newsitem.title: UK: Woman dies in new Scots food poisoning outbreak.
newsitem.headline: Woman dies in new Scots food poisoning outbreak.

text.p: A new outbreak of E coli food poisoning, which killed 18 old people in Scotland late last year, has carried off a woman in her 90s, health officials said on Friday.
Five more old people were taken ill in the outbreak, which the officials said was not related to the earlier epidemic.
The dead woman and four of the five were living in a nursing home in Arbroath on the east coast of Scotland.
Dr Mike Rowarth, a public health expert at the local Tayside Health Board, said urgent investigations were under way to discover the source of the outbreak.
"I think at the moment, with the five cases that we have in the nursing home...we think that is probably what we call a point source," he told BBC radio.
"That means they have all probably been infected at the same time, probably by something that has gone wrong in the kitchen."
He said he doubted Scotland had any particular problem with food poisoning, despite the publicity surrounding the last outbreak, one of the deadliest in the world.
"There is a background level of E coli and most of the cases we see are sporadic," Rowarth said.
"Whether we have a truly raised incidence in Scotland is a matter of debate."
E coli, only identified in the 1980s, is a mutated version of a common gut bacteria. It gets into food via improper slaughtering techniques or the use of manure as fertiliser.
It can make a healthy adult ill but can cause kidney failure and brain damage in vulnerable victims such as the elderly and young children.
